### svc-nixl · 2026-09-15

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-non-gpu` · commit `40cf77c7`

**TL;DR:** Three of the six `Build` variants died in `meson setup` because the `taskflow` subproject wrap does a live `git clone https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow.git` and git got an auth prompt ("could not read Username for 'https://github.com'"); convert `subprojects/taskflow.wrap` to a `[wrap-file]` tarball (like `liburing.wrap`) or pre-install taskflow in the CI images.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** `nixl-ci-non-gpu` #3050 — stages 358, 424 and 440 ("Build") failed during `meson setup nixl_build` with `meson.build:233:16: ERROR: Git command failed: [... 'clone', '--depth', '1', '--branch', 'v3.10.0', 'https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow.git', 'taskflow']`.

**Root cause:** `meson.build:233` resolves `dependency('taskflow', fallback: ['taskflow', 'taskflow_dep'])`, and `subprojects/taskflow.wrap` is a `[wrap-git]` wrap, so meson must perform a live `git clone` from github.com at configure time. On the three failing containers that clone was rejected and git fell back to prompting for credentials:
```
Cloning into 'taskflow'...
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address
fatal: expected flush after ref listing
```
In the same log, plain HTTPS artifact downloads in those very containers *did* work (`Downloading liburing source from https://github.com/axboe/liburing/archive/...` succeeded), and in the passing variants (e.g. stage 383) the identical clone succeeded and reported `Dependency taskflow from subproject subprojects/taskflow found: YES 3.10.0`. So this is not a code defect and not a total network outage — it is an unauthenticated `git clone` to github being intermittently refused (rate-limit/proxy), and the build has no fallback for it. No hang is involved: the failing stages died 5–11 s in, within seconds of the clone attempt.

**Implicated commit:** 76275cfc — "Use tagged Taskflow git wrap for NIXL builds (#2121)", bzsuni (introduced the `[wrap-git]` taskflow wrap). The build's own commit 40cf77c7 is unrelated to the failure.

**File:** `subprojects/taskflow.wrap:1-4` (triggered from `meson.build:233`)

**Suggested fix:** Replace the git wrap with a hash-pinned tarball wrap so it uses the same HTTPS path that already works, and keep the existing patch directory, e.g.:
```ini
[wrap-file]
directory = taskflow-3.10.0
source_url = https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow/archive/refs/tags/v3.10.0.tar.gz
source_filename = taskflow-3.10.0.tar.gz
source_hash = <sha256 of the release tarball>
source_fallback_url = <internal/wrapdb mirror>
patch_directory = taskflow

[provide]
taskflow = taskflow_dep
```
Better still (and consistent with how abseil/UCX are handled in these `PRE_INSTALLED_ENV` images): install taskflow headers into the CI base images so `dependency('taskflow')` is found via pkg-config/cmake and no network fetch happens at all, and/or pre-populate `subprojects/packagecache` in the image. Re-running #3050 will likely pass, but the flake will recur until the git clone is removed from the configure path.

**Related:** none found (searches for the taskflow clone error returned no matching issues/PRs).

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-15

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` · commit `40cf77c7`

**TL;DR:** The container build dies at `uv pip install torch` because the Dockerfile derives the PyTorch wheel index from `CUDA_VERSION` and the new CUDA 13.4 base image yields `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu134`, a channel PyTorch never published — pin/clamp the torch index to a real channel (e.g. `cu130`) with a PyPI fallback instead of computing it from `CUDA_VERSION`.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** All four parallel "Build image" stages of `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` #644 failed; the x86_64 variants failed at Dockerfile STEP 53/72 (`uv pip install --system torch torchvision torchaudio`), the aarch64 variant failed earlier at STEP 31/72 (`git clone` of abseil).

**Root cause:** Two separate failures, one deterministic and one transient:

1. **Deterministic (primary).** `contrib/Dockerfile:336` builds the index URL as `UV_INDEX="https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu$(echo $CUDA_VERSION | cut -d. -f1,2 | tr -d .)"`. The base image is now `nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda-dl-base:26.08-cuda13.4-devel-ubuntu24.04`, so `CUDA_VERSION=13.4` → `cu134`. That channel does not exist as a real PyTorch wheel index, so uv resolved only stale artifacts and aborted:
   ```
   error: No solution found when resolving dependencies
     cause: Because all versions of torch have no wheels with a matching Python ABI tag (e.g., `cp312`) ...
   hint: `torch` was found on https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu134, but not at the requested version
   hint: You require CPython 3.12 (`cp312`), but we only found wheels for `torch` (v2.0.1) with ... `cp38`, `cp39`, `cp310`, `cp311`
   subprocess exited with status 1
   ```
   Because `UV_INDEX` is set, uv also refuses to fall back to PyPI (dependency-confusion guard), so there is no recovery path. The base image also ships no system torch, so the `import torch` guard on line 333 takes the install branch every time. This will fail on every build until the index expression is fixed.

2. **Transient (aarch64 stage, node 107).** Anonymous clone of Abseil was rejected by GitHub:
   ```
   Cloning into 'abseil-cpp'...
   fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address
   fatal: expected flush after ref listing
   Error: building at STEP "RUN git clone https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp.git ..." : exit status 128
   ```
   A public clone should never prompt for credentials; this signature is GitHub returning 401/429 (unauthenticated rate limit or an egress proxy hiccup). Note the same build cloned `gtest-parallel` successfully seconds later on another node, and this step has no retry — a single rate-limited request kills a 40-minute image build.

**Implicated commit:** `[REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String]` — "build: bump CUDA and CI base images, stop restating them across CI (#2205)", NirWolfer, 2026-09-10. It moved the base to `cuda13.4`, which is what turns the previously-valid computed index into `cu134`.

**File:** `contrib/Dockerfile:336` (torch index derivation; guard at :333, base tag at :17/:23). Secondary: `contrib/Dockerfile:157` (unretried `git clone`).

**Suggested fix:**
1. Stop deriving the channel arithmetically. Introduce an explicit, reviewable ARG and use it, so a CUDA bump can't silently invent a channel:
   ```dockerfile
   ARG TORCH_INDEX_URL="https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130"
   RUN if python${DEFAULT_PYTHON_VERSION} -c "import torch; v=torch.__version__.split('.')[:2]; assert (int(v[0]),int(v[1])) >= (2,7)" 2>/dev/null; then \
           echo "Using PyTorch from system site-packages"; \
       else \
           uv pip install --system --index-strategy unsafe-best-match \
               --extra-index-url "${TORCH_INDEX_URL}" torch torchvision torchaudio; \
       fi
   ```
   Using `--extra-index-url` + `unsafe-best-match` keeps PyPI as a fallback so a missing channel degrades instead of hard-failing. If a CUDA-13.4-specific channel is genuinely required, verify it is published before bumping `BASE_IMAGE_TAG`.
2. Add retry/backoff to the source clones (Abseil, gRPC, etcd, gusli, aws-sdk, azure-sdk) — e.g. wrap in a `for i in 1 2 3; do git clone ... && break; sleep 15; done` helper, or pass a token/use an internal mirror for `github.com` to avoid unauthenticated rate limits on aarch64 runners.

**Related:** #2205 (CUDA/base-image bump that introduced the `cu134` index); #2250 "build: bump DOCA to 3.5" touches the same base-image ARGs and will hit the identical torch failure.

</details>
